DISCOVER THE JOY OF TEACHING
In a time when many teachers are feeling dissatisfied or undervalued, OneSchool Global offers something truly different: an environment designed to help both students and teachers thrive.
At OneSchool Global you will discover the joy of teaching in a unique, supportive environment that values your professional growth and development. Our innovative approach to education emphasises self-directed learning, where students take the initiative and responsibility for their learning journey, reducing the need for constant behavioural management and allowing you to focus on meaningful teaching. Open to educators from all backgrounds, OneSchool provides an inclusive, respectful atmosphere that fosters collaboration and growth, ensuring that every teacher feels valued and supported as a part of our global community.

OneSchool Global educator crowned Australian Teacher Aide of the Year
Our People
Australia
Toowoomba
SHARE
A OneSchool Global educator who has transformed learning experiences for students with diverse learning needs has been named the 2026 Australian Teacher Aide of the Year, with the announcement providing a fitting highlight during Teacher Aide Week.
Kimberley Nolan, Campus Student Support Assistant at OneSchool Global Toowoomba, received the national honour after first being recognised as the 2026 Queensland Teacher Aide of the Year, recognising her as the top teacher aide in the state.
The award recognises teacher aides who demonstrate exceptional impact on student learning, wellbeing and inclusion, with Kimberley’s work highlighted for both its measurable outcomes and the care she brings to supporting students every day. The awards recognised Kimberley’s results in improving individual learning goals, literacy and numeracy outcomes.
Kimberley said the recognition reflected the students and school community she works alongside every day.
“I absolutely love walking into my campus each and every day knowing I can make a difference. I am supported by incredible staff, students and families. I am so fortunate to have a workplace and job that I absolutely love”.
Throughout her nomination, colleagues described Kimberley as a highly proactive educator who consistently goes beyond the expectations of her role to support students and staff.
Wendy Robinson, Sub-Regional Director of Learning Support for QLD, said Kimberley exemplified the very best of teacher aide practice.
“Kimberley exemplifies the very best of teacher aide practice through her deeply student-centred approach, outstanding professionalism and lasting impact on the students she supports.”
Toowoomba Campus Principal James Easthope said Kimberley’s influence extended across every aspect of campus life.
“Kimberley consistently goes above and beyond her role description, providing exceptional support to both staff and students. She proactively develops and shares high-quality resources, offers targeted in-class assistance and plays a key role in creating a positive campus culture.”
Kimberley’s national title capped a remarkable result for OneSchool Global in the 2026 Australian Teacher Aide Awards. In addition to her Queensland and Australian Teacher Aide of the Year honours, the Orange Campus Learning Support Team was recognised among the national Team of the Year nominees, while the Melton OneSchool Campus Learning Support Team received a Highly Commended award. The results reflect the depth of expertise within OneSchool Global’s learning support teams and their commitment to helping every student thrive.
About OneSchool Global OneSchool Global is an independent school network that has more than 8,000 primary and secondary students and 2,000 staff across the globe, in regions including United Kingdom, North America, Europe, Australia, Argentina, New Zealand and the Caribbean. Our students come from the Plymouth Brethren Christian Church community; however, OneSchool Global is not a religious school and only teaches religion as required in the curriculum.

OSG educators share back-to-school insights with teachers across North America
North America
Teaching and Learning
SHARE
As a new school year begins across North America, OneSchool Global educators are helping fellow teachers start with confidence and maintain it throughout the school year.
Drawing on the expertise of teachers, principals and school leaders from across the OSG North America network, a recent nationally distributed media feature highlighted practical back-to-school advice designed to support educators as they prepare for a new academic year. The story was subsequently syndicated across a range of online news platforms.
The press release, “Eight School Year’s Resolutions for Teachers’, highlights simple but meaningful habits that can help teachers feel more organised, energised and prepared for the year ahead.
Contributors included educators from OSG campuses in New York and Tennessee, alongside regional school leadership, who shared practical strategies for creating engaging classrooms, fostering student ownership, supporting professional growth and building strong school cultures.
Among the ideas featured were encouraging curiosity through thoughtful questioning, creating opportunities for students to take greater ownership of their learning, celebrating small wins and making time for professional reflection and development.
Jonathon Borys, Regional Head of School at OneSchool Global North America, said many of the most valuable ideas in education come from teachers themselves.
“You’re not going to get everything right the first time. What matters is being willing to learn from it, make a change, and keep moving forward.”
The feature reflects OneSchool Global’s commitment to sharing educational best practice and contributing to broader conversations about teaching and learning.
With more than 120 campuses across 20 countries, OneSchool Global is uniquely positioned to bring together insights from educators working in diverse contexts, while remaining united by a shared goal: helping students develop the skills, confidence and independence they need to be life-ready.
So, what were the tips?

OneSchool Global recognised with Gold at the international Symbol Awards
SHARE
OneSchool Global has been awarded Gold in the Sustainable Workplace Culture Program category at the international Symbol Awards, recognising the organisation’s commitment to creating a workplace where educators and staff can grow, lead and perform at their best.
The global award recognises organisations that have built strong, sustainable workplace cultures that support employee wellbeing, professional growth and long-term organisational success.
For OneSchool Global, the gold Symbol Award reflects a deliberate focus on investing in people across its global network of more than 120 campuses in 20 countries. Through initiatives such as the Global Teacher Academy, the Persona 360 degree feedback program, the Kudos recognition platform and a wide range of People & Culture initiatives, OSG has continued to strengthen employee engagement, leadership development and professional growth opportunities.
The awarding body acknowledged the breadth programs and initiatives across the organisation, including increased staff engagement, reduced employee turnover, strong participation in professional learning and a growing culture of recognition and collaboration.
Global Head of People and Culture, Ashley Woolnough said the award reflected the collective efforts of staff across the organisation.
“This recognition belongs to the people of OneSchool Global. Every day, our staff create a learning environment where students can thrive, while also supporting one another through collaboration, professional growth and a shared commitment to excellence.”
“We believe that when people are provided with clarity, opportunity and support, they are empowered to make a meaningful impact. This award is an acknowledgement of the culture our teams have built together across our global network.”
The Symbol Awards celebrate excellence in business, innovation and performance from across the globe. Receiving Gold in the Sustainable Workplace Culture Program category places OneSchool Global among leading organisations recognised for creating positive, high-performing workplaces.
Lean more about the awards and the 2026 winners here: https://symbolawards.com/winners2026

pageCache.pageTitle: Our School | OneSchool Global Learning Community
pageCache.text:
Discover a POSITIVE DIFFERENCE
Creating an environment in which we nurture teachers to become leaders of learning.
OneSchool Global offers a distinctive and progressive educational experience that prepares students to be life-ready, not just career-ready. By emphasising self-directed learning, innovative teaching methods, and a supportive school culture, OSG ensures that both teachers and students can achieve their full potential in a dynamic and modern educational setting.
Our progressive teaching philosophy
At OneSchool Global, our Learning to Learn Framework is a self-directed learning philosophy, based on international research and best practice, that enables students to take ownership of their learning. We encourage critical thinking and independent learning, and embed problem-solving skills to prepare students to adapt and succeed in a rapidly changing world. Not only does our student-centred model of education create an engaging and empowering learning environment, we believe that it sets the standard for modern education, and it is increasingly recognised as such.
A more supportive environment
OneSchool is committed to nurturing teachers to become ‘leaders of learning’ through professional development programs and leadership opportunities. Our Teacher Academy provides onboarding support, training, resources and global collaboration that will help you excel in your role, and our supportive leadership and culture ensures that every teacher feels valued and equipped to inspire their students.
Inside the Global Teacher Academy
The Global Teacher Academy (GTA) is OneSchool Global’s internal teaching faculty providing training, networking, and support for all teachers. New teachers undergo a globally consistent induction program, followed by mentorship from experienced teachers. Throughout the year, there are multiple professional development sessions, both in-person and via Zoom, covering topics like real-world applications of the Learning to Learn Framework. The Global Teacher Academy is a key part of how our teachers ‘rediscover the joy of teaching’.
Smaller classes with less behaviour to manage
With smaller class sizes, teachers at OneSchool can provide more attention and support to each student, enhancing learning outcomes and also reducing the time spent on behaviour management. This, combined with our self-motivated students, means our teachers are able to fully focus on being the best teachers they can be.
Fully contemporary classrooms
OneSchool’s classrooms are modern learning environments equipped with state-of-the-art technology. From video conferencing facilities to individual student laptops, our schools provide the tools necessary for a fully contemporary educational experience. This supports our Learning to Learn Framework and ensures that students are well-prepared for the digital world we all live in.
A vision and values we can all share
OneSchool Global’s vision is to be a global education ecosystem that develops life ready students who learn how to learn and achieve.
Our values of integrity, care & compassion, respect, responsibility, and commitment are at the core of everything we do. These values, inspired by Christian teachings, are universal and shared by educators and students from all backgrounds. By fostering a culture driven by these values, we create the positive and inclusive conditions required for everyone to thrive.
The Plymouth Brethren Christian Church
OneSchool Global is an independent network of schools attended by families of the Plymouth Brethren Christian Church. While originally established by members of the Church and underpinned by a Christian ethos, the school is not a religious institution and is not owned or operated by the Church.
The Plymouth Brethren Christian Church Community has over 55,000 members across Australia, New Zealand, Europe, the Americas and the UK.
Members of the Church are deeply family-oriented and live, work and pray as ‘Brethren’ – a community of families held together by common Christian beliefs. There is a strong charitable spirit among the Church Community, with many devoting their time to philanthropic efforts, particularly through the work of the charity, Rapid Relief Team (RRT).
The Church Community and OneSchool staff enjoy a strong working relationship, with strong support from Church Community volunteers. Watch the video to the right to discover what it’s like working alongside the Brethren community.

pageCache.pageTitle: OneSchool Global students raise $100,000 to support sick kids - One School Global

OneSchool Global students raise $100,000 to support sick kids
Australia
Students
Fundraising
SHARE
Students from seven Victorian OneSchool Global (OSG) campuses have joined forces to raise more than $100,000 for the Royal Children’s Hospital Foundation (RCHF), supporting vital healthcare investments for kids in need.
From car washes to food festivals, our students embraced creativity and teamwork to rally the support of our school community in recent months, reaching their ambitious target on the back of passion and purpose.
The incredible donation was presented to the Royal Children’s Hospital in Melbourne on Monday 17 August at a special event attended by OSG Regional Principal, Mr Frank Vetere, and senior students from the school.
Meaningful impact, driven by our Student Leadership Teams
All seven Victorian OneSchool Global campuses – Bairnsdale, Bendigo, Berwick, Hamilton, Melton, Nathalia, and Swan Hill – were involved in this initiative, showcasing the collaboration and camaraderie which the school is renowned for.
Mr Frank Vetere, Regional Principal, said the fundraising effort was testament to the students’ hard work and the generosity of the school community.
“We’ve been supporting the Royal Children’s Hospital Foundation for a few years now, but in 2026 we have gone to a new level, raising more than $100,000 for the first time. I’m so proud of our Student Leadership Teams who have spearheaded this initiative with such enthusiasm, dedication and commitment. I also want to thank everyone from the school community who donated for their generosity.”
Mr Vetere also called out the school’s innovative approach to learning which encourages students to be ‘life-ready’ and prepared to tackle challenging tasks that come their way.
“Through our self-directed learning model, students are empowered to take control of their learning – and that proactive nature shines through in initiatives like this, where they have the confidence and skill to execute a fundraising project of this scale.”
Coming together to make a difference
Each campus involved found innovative ways to raise funds, which helped drive the positive response from the school community.
Swan Hill campus students ran a car wash, ensuring every vehicle that came through was sparkling clean, while students from Hamilton, Bendigo and Nathalia campuses held multicultural fetes with a feast of international delights on offer. Students at the Melton and Berwick campuses hosted carnival-style festivals and our Bairnsdale students held a Bikeathon to stay fit and raise money at the same time.
“Kudos to our student leadership teams for coming up with clever and creative ways to raise funds in an engaging manner, which added a layer of enjoyment to their outstanding fundraising efforts,” Mr Vetere added.
Building a tradition of giving
At the donation presentation, the Royal Children’s Hospital Foundation’s Deputy Director of Fundraising, Kathryn Sell, praised OneSchool Global’s ongoing support of the hospital.
“OneSchool Global students have raised more than $400,000 for the RCHF in recent years, which is truly remarkable. This donation will be directed to our Children’s Cancer Centre, which provides care, treatment and improved quality of life for kids with cancer. We’re so grateful for the support and would like to sincerely thank everyone who made this donation possible.”
